newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rolls-Royce sees new airliner demand at over 600.
newsitem.headline: Rolls-Royce sees new airliner demand at over 600.

text.p: The chairman of British engineering group Rolls-Royce Plc told a news conference on Thursday that he expects demand for the next generation of large-capacity four-engined airliners to be more than 600 units.
"We believe 600 plus," Ralph Robins said on a visit to Tokyo. "We think we will get more than half of the market."

Rolls-Royce has been developing a new 80,000-lb thrust engine called the Trent 900 designed to power the next-generation large capacity airliners. It announced on Tuesday that Japan's Kawasaki Heavy Industries would take a six-percent share in the new engine programme.
Asked about the recently agreed merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp Robins said:
"We are very content because it will strengthen some of McDonnell Douglas' programmes in the military area."
He said that if Japanese airlines selected Rolls-Royce engines the firm was ready to invest in building facilities in Japan for maintenance and spare parts.
He said Rolls-Royce currently has no such facilities in Japan as Japanese airlines have not purchased Rolls-Royce engines for some time.
Robins came to Japan for talks with government and industry officials.
